key_concepts: Meiosis consists of two cell divisions that produce four gametes.
Each meiotic division passes through prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase.
Meiosis I separates homologous chromosome pairs.
Gametes are sperm in males and eggs in females.
Somatic body cells have 46 chromosomes arranged in 23 homologous pairs.
Homologous chromosomes carry alleles for the same genes at corresponding positions.
Sperm and egg cells are haploid, containing 23 chromosomes each.
Fertilization fuses a sperm and egg to restore the full set of 46 chromosomes.
Meiosis produces genetically distinct haploid cells, contributing to variation among offsp
